lesson.title: Setting the Scene: Preterite vs Imperfect
lesson.subtitle: The background canvas (estaba, vivía, era) interrupted by the event dot (llegó, vi, fue)

hook.title: Stage Lighting vs The Actor Entering
hook.content:
Every great story uses both past tenses together:
• **Imperfect (Stage Lighting & Scenery)**: Estaba en el restaurante ('I was in the restaurant'), el café estaba caliente ('the coffee was hot'), la noche era hermosa ('the night was beautiful').
• **Preterite (The Action on Stage)**: Hablé con mi amigo ('I spoke with my friend'), comí el pastel ('I ate the cake'), fue un éxito ('it was a success' — summing up the whole finished event as one dot)!

pattern.title: Why 'Era' Paints the Ongoing Quality and 'Fue' Judges the Completed Event
pattern.content: Notice the difference: La fiesta era grande ('The party was big' — describing what it looked like while you were in the middle of it) vs La fiesta fue un éxito ('The party was a success' — stamping a final verdict on the finished event)!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: I was in the hotel (background location)
he went to the hotel (event dot)
it was a big house (ongoing description)
it was a success (final verdict on finished event)
I was speaking (ongoing) vs I spoke (completed)

exercises.target_answer: estaba en el hotel, fue al hotel, era una casa grande, fue un éxito, hablaba vs hablé
exercises.meaning: I was in the hotel (background location), he went to the hotel (event dot), it was a big house (ongoing description), it was a success (final verdict on finished event), I was speaking (ongoing) vs I spoke (completed)
exercises.explanation: Imperfect puts you inside the ongoing moment; preterite steps back and views the completed event as a whole.

exercises.prompt: In 'I was at the house when I spoke with my mother', which pair of verbs matches 'was' (background location) and 'spoke' (completed event)?
exercises.explanation: Estaba sets the ongoing location; hablé marks the completed conversation.

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'I was at the restaurant and I ate the cake'
exercises.target_answer: Estaba en el restaurante y comí el pastel
exercises.meaning: I was at the restaurant and I ate the cake

exercises.idea: say that the hotel was very good (ongoing description) and yesterday you spoke with your friend
cues: The hotel was very good → El hotel era muy bueno
and yesterday I spoke → y ayer hablé
with my friend → con mi amigo
idea_parts: The hotel was very good → El hotel era muy bueno
and yesterday I spoke with my friend → y ayer hablé con mi amigo
exercises.target_answer: El hotel era muy bueno y ayer hablé con mi amigo
exercises.meaning: The hotel was very good and yesterday I spoke with my friend
exercises.explanation: El hotel era muy bueno (description) + y ayer hablé con mi amigo (event).

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.meaning: I was here and it was fantastic
cues: and it was fantastic (verdict): y fue fantástico
exercises.affirmation: Masterful contrast of estaba and fue!

summary.outcome: Combine imperfect background descriptions (era, estaba, hablaba) with preterite events (hablé, comí, fue).

use_example.german: Estaba en Madrid, la ciudad era hermosa y fue un viaje fantástico.
use_example.english: I was in Madrid, the city was beautiful, and it was a fantastic trip.

summary.takeaway: Imperfect = inside the ongoing scene (era, estaba, hablaba); Preterite = the completed event or final verdict (hablé, comí, fue).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([20] desde hace & Present Duration): see why actions that started in the past and continue right now stay in the PRESENT tense!

twist.prompt: Assemble: 'I was speaking when he went'

estaba.english_meaning: I / he / she / it was (imperfect of estar)

era.english_meaning: I / he / she / it was (imperfect of ser)
era.context_phrase: Cuando era joven, vivía en Madrid.
era.context_translation: When I was young, I lived in Madrid.
era.etymology_derivation: Latin erat — English 'era' (an ongoing epoch of time) is the exact same root!

hablaba.english_meaning: I / he / she was speaking, used to speak
hablaba.context_phrase: Cuando vivía allí, hablaba español todos los días.
hablaba.context_translation: When I lived there, I spoke Spanish every day.
hablaba.etymology_derivation: Every -ar verb takes -aba in the imperfect with zero irregulars!

fue.english_cognate: was / went (shared preterite of ser & ir!)
fue.shift_rule: Shared preterite of ser and ir (fui, fuiste, fue)
fue.etymology_derivation: ser ('to be') and ir ('to go') share the exact same preterite forms: fui ('I was / I went'), fue ('it was / he went')!

hablé.context_translation: Yesterday I spoke with my mother.
hablé.etymology_derivation: Notice how the accent mark carries the entire tense difference: hablo ('I speak') vs. habló ('he/she spoke')!

comí.context_translation: Yesterday I ate at that restaurant.

casa.etymology_derivation: Latin casa originally meant a cottage, replacing domus in everyday Romance speech.

hotel.etymology_derivation: Silent initial H. Latin hospitāle gives both 'hospital' and 'hotel'.
